supplementary_artifacts.note: Food-level concentration tables (Appendices 10-11) are only in this appendices volume; the main report PDF contains methods and summaries.

disposition_reason: The 23rd ATDS analysed one in-scope cocoa food, 'Chocolate, milk' (4 composites of 3 retail purchases each), for Al, total As, Cd, Pb, total Hg and Cr; food-level means, medians and min/max are printed in the appendices. Chocolate was not analysed for inorganic As, inorganic Hg or MeHg (those were fish/shellfish only).
disposition_locator: Appendices Tables A10.1, A10.2, A10.4, A10.5, A10.7, A11.2 (PDF pp.45-90); main report pp.15-16 (sampling) and Appendix 5 Table A5.1 (methods/LOR)

study.material_scope: retail milk chocolate analysed as purchased (TDS 'national food')
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Purchase market Australia (two capital cities); cocoa growing origin not reported
study.sampling_unit: composite samples, each of three primary retail purchases from a single state/territory (national foods: 2 composites x 2 capital cities)
study.method: Microwave digestion with ultra-pure nitric acid; Al by ICP-AES; As, Cd, Pb, total Hg by ICP-MS; Cr by ICP-AES/ICP-MS (Symbio Alliance)

lod_loq.tHg: not separately stated for total Hg in Table A5.1 (0.025 mg/kg* shown is for methyl/inorganic Hg speciation)

study.basis: table-ready composite (milk chocolate analysed as purchased; no preparation instruction listed in Appendix 3), wet/as-consumed weight
study.qa: LOD = LOR for all contaminants and nutrients; LOR varies by matrix. No CRM/recovery data for chocolate reported in the appendices.

findings.integrity_issue: Mean(nd=1/2LOR) 0.23 minus mean(nd=0) 0.16 = 0.07 mg/kg implies 1/2LOR = 0.28 mg/kg (LOR ~0.56 mg/kg) for the single non-detect, which exceeds the Table A6.1 chromium LOR range (0.0005-0.025 mg/kg) and the reported maximum 0.27 mg/kg; with LOR <=0.025 the two means should differ by <=0.003 mg/kg. The printed means cannot both be correct.

notes: Out-of-scope cocoa-containing composite foods also tabulated: 'Cake, chocolate, iced' (all metals) . Consumption/exposure tables use the food group 'Chocolates, cocoa and fudge' (milk chocolate mapped to 'Cocoa; chocolate; chocolate bars; chocolate coated-confectionery and fudge (excluding those with fruit, nuts, biscuit or coconut)', Table A13.1); these are exposure context, not occurrence. Table A22.5 shows 'Chocolates, cocoa and fudge' contributing up to 7-8% of cobalt intake (cobalt not tracked). The 25th ATDS (Tables 6 and 7) re-quotes this study's milk chocolate means as Cd 0.042 and Pb 0.028 mg/kg, consistent with this extraction.
contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary does not report any milk chocolate occurrence values; it lists only chocolate cake aluminium (87.9 mg/kg median), which is an out-of-scope composite food.
Stored summary metals list omits chromium, although chromium was measured in milk chocolate (Table A11.2).
Stored summary routes iAs/MeHg/iHg generally; the primary shows these were analysed only in fish/shellfish, not chocolate.
unresolved: Chromium mean (nd=1/2LOR) of 0.23 mg/kg is arithmetically inconsistent with the stated LOR range and the 0.16 mg/kg lower-bound mean (see integrity_issue); the individual composite values are not printed, so the correct value cannot be recovered.
Total mercury LOR for chocolate is not stated in Table A5.1 (only the speciation LOR 0.025 mg/kg).
